description: Measure a vehicle's overhead clearance along a route against surveyed point cloud geometry, wherever survey coverage exists. Routes with truck costing (so the search already avoids the height restrictions the map has tagged), then measures that corridor. Give `origin`, `destination` and `height_m`; optional `width_m` asks the corridor-width axis too, and optional `margin_m` adds your operating margin to the vehicle before the verdict. Returns `pass`, `fail`, `indeterminate` or `no_verdict` with the limiting point, the measured headroom, its uncertainty bound (`safe_headroom_m`, `sigma_m`, `sampling_gap_m`) and a link to that exact view in the survey viewer. An `indeterminate` carries `indeterminate_reasons` as codes to branch on and the same reasons as English inside `explanation`; read out the English. A `pass` may carry no limiting point at all, which means the survey found nothing above that corridor, and the width axis may answer `not_assessed` where the corridor edges are too sparsely surveyed while the height axis still answers. Honesty, and it matters here: this measures physical geometry from a dated survey. It is not a signed or posted height, `clearance_enforcement.route_certified` is always false, and the caveat is on every answer including the clear one. Ground the survey did not cover comes back as `not_surveyed_m` and is never judged, so a `pass` is possible over complete coverage and nowhere else; sparse or stale coverage comes back separately as `insufficient_data_m`. Reach for this when a truck route came back unchanged and you need to know whether that means anything: an unchanged route avoids what the map records, which is a different claim from measured headroom, because a structure nobody tagged is routed through like open road. Needs the MapMap gateway (GATEWAY_URL + GATEWAY_API_KEY), which holds the surveys; there is no fallback, and it will not answer from the routing step alone. The mapmap://guide/clearance resource sets out what each answer proves.

LatLon.description: A WGS84 coordinate in decimal degrees: a {lat, lon} object (preferred), or a GeoJSON [lon, lat] array with LONGITUDE FIRST, the same order as every polygon field on this server.

height_m.description:
Vehicle height in metres. Required: there is no default vehicle,
because a default vehicle is how somebody gets an answer about a
lorry that is not theirs.

margin_m.description:
Operating margin in metres, added to the height before the verdict
is decided (default 0). Your compliance policy, not ours: the
measured figure and the safe bound are both reported whatever you
set here, and the margin is echoed back. It is applied to the
measurement, not to the routing step, where the map's own posted
heights already carry a margin of their own.

width_m.description:
Vehicle width in metres. Supplying it asks the width axis as well as
the height axis; the width answer is reported separately and is
never a headroom.

name: check_clearance_on_route

ClearanceDatasetSummary.description: One survey the report drew on.

stale.description:
Whether the clearance field lags the survey it was baked from, or
has never been checked against it. Either way no route passes on it.

ClearanceEnforcement.description:
How a clearance answer was arrived at, and what it therefore does and
does not prove.

The [`TunnelEnforcement`] pattern, applied to the other safety-adjacent
answer this server gives, and for the same reason: a headroom figure
with a bound on it reads like permission. It is not one. The block is
carried on every response including the clear one, because the clear one
is the dangerous one.

Every field is taken verbatim from the gateway's report rather than
rebuilt here. `vertical_datum` is a property of the survey the figures
came from, so this server cannot know it; and copying the caveat text
into a second crate is exactly the drift the single-source-of-truth rule
exists to prevent. When the gateway omits any part of it, the tool
refuses the answer rather than emitting a report with a hollow caveat.

basis.description:
How the figures were arrived at. Always
`"surveyed_pointcloud_within_survey_difference"`: the difference
between two heights measured in the same survey, on the same date,
by the same processing. No map tag, no terrain model and no absolute
vertical datum enters it.

caveat.description: What this answer does and does not prove, in one paragraph.

route_certified.description:
Whether the route has been certified against a structure inventory.
Always `false`, and there is no future in which it is true: this is
a measurement with a bound, never a certificate about a route.

vertical_datum.description:
The vertical frame the surveyed figures live in, spelled for a
reader.

ClearanceWidthSummary.description:
The width axis: how wide the clear corridor is, never how tall.

A separate type from [`LimitingPointSummary`] on purpose, with no
headroom field on it. These are different physical quantities, and a
shared type is how the reader of a width answer ends up quoting a
headroom.

clear_width_m.description:
Free width of the narrowest clear corridor found, metres. Present
where a corridor edge was actually measured.

reason.description:
Why the width axis declined to answer, present for
`not_assessed`.

safe_clear_width_m.description:
That width less its uncertainty terms, metres: the number the width
verdict is decided on.

verdict.description:
`pass`, `fail`, `indeterminate`, `no_verdict`, or `not_assessed`
where the geometry or the request did not support an answer.

LimitingPointSummary.description:
One measured clearance on the route, with the bounds that qualify it.

There is no field here for a posted, signed or otherwise legally
binding height, and that absence is deliberate. A survey measures the
physical gap; a sign records a restriction a road authority posted, set
below the physical gap on purpose. They are different quantities and
this server never reports one as the other.

dataset.description: The dataset the measurement came from.

headroom_m.description:
Measured headroom: the surveyed gap between the road surface and
the lowest validated surface above it, metres.

lat.description: Latitude of the point, decimal degrees.

lon.description: Longitude of the point, decimal degrees.

overhead_class.description:
What the overhead surface is made of: `structure`, `vegetation`,
`wire` or `unknown`. Foliage is compressible and seasonal, so an old
reading of it stops deciding.

route_distance_m.description: How far along the route the point sits, metres.

safe_headroom_m.description:
`headroom_m` less the uncertainty terms, metres. This is the number
the verdict is decided on, and the number to plan against.

sampling_gap_m.description:
One-sided sampling bias bound, metres: how far below the lowest
sample the true low point could hang, given the sample spacing.

sigma_m.description: One-sigma measurement uncertainty on that figure, metres.

surveyed_on.description: Last capture date of the survey behind this measurement, ISO.

advisories.description:
Notes on stretches of the route: vegetation age, a reading limited
by a wire, a seam between surveys.

assessed_m.description:
Metres of route measured against survey data good enough to decide
on.

clearance_enforcement.description: What this answer does and does not prove. Read it.

datasets.description: The surveys drawn on, with their capture dates and staleness.

explanation.description:
What was measured, when, with what bound, and what the tool declined
to conclude. It may over-restrict; it never under-restricts.

geometry_polyline6.description:
The route as a six-digit-precision encoded polyline, so the same
shape can be drawn or re-measured without routing again.

indeterminate_reasons.description:
Why an `indeterminate` could not be called, as machine-readable
codes (`inside_uncertainty_band`, `vegetation_age_exceeded`,
`artefact_stale`, `artefact_freshness_unchecked`). Empty on every
other verdict. These are for branching on, not for reading out: the
same reasons appear as English in `explanation`, and a person shown
`artefact_freshness_unchecked` has been failed by whatever displayed
it.

insufficient_data_m.description:
Metres of route a survey covers but too sparsely, or too stale, to
decide on. Also an absence, and reported apart from
`not_surveyed_m` because the two have different remedies.

limiting.description:
The limiting point on a `fail`, the tightest point on a `pass`, the
worst contested point on an `indeterminate`. Absent on a
`no_verdict`, and absent on a `pass` where the survey found nothing
at all above the corridor.

not_surveyed_m.description:
Metres of route no survey covers. This is the absence of a
measurement, and it is never the same statement as a measured open
sky. No verdict is drawn over it.

resolution_hint.description:
What would resolve an `indeterminate`, in one sentence, as the
measuring service phrased it.

route_distance_m.description: Length of the route the vehicle was routed over, metres.

route_duration_s.description: Estimated driving time for that route, seconds.

verdict.description:
`pass`, `fail`, `indeterminate` or `no_verdict` for the height axis.
A `pass` is possible over completely surveyed ground and nowhere
else: unsurveyed ground yields `no_verdict`, never a pass.

view_url.description:
Deep link to that exact view in the survey viewer, so the reading
can be looked at rather than taken on trust.

width.description: The width axis, answered separately when `width_m` was given.
